Article Title: 'CBI probe into Ajit Pawar's death, name Pune Ring Road after him,' Rohit Pawar urges Amit Shah
Article Text:
Rohit Pawar seeks a CBI probe into Ajit Pawar's death

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Sunday urged Union home minister Amit Shah to announce a CBI probe into the death of former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar and name Pune's Ring Road after the late leader. This came as Shah is on a two-day visit to Pune and is set to unveil a statue of Ajit Pawar."Rather than limiting Dada’s achievements to merely unveiling a statue, it would be better if Shah announced that the Pune ring road would be named after Ajit Dada and that the CBI would investigate Dada’s accident. Otherwise, we will launch a major agitation to get the ring road named after him on the anniversary of Dada’s death..!" he said in a post on X.Shah is scheduled to unveil a statue of Ajit Pawar at the Pune Zilla Parishad office on Monday.The NCP (SP) legislator thanked the district council leaders who supported the installation of the statue but questioned why state ministers who had benefited from Ajit Pawar's political support were not demanding that the Ring Road be named after him."I understand that Union Home Minister Amit Shah will unveil a statue of Ajit Dada in Pune. Thanks to him for unveiling a statue erected by district council leaders who revere Dada, given that Dada’s party is in power in the Pune district council! But don’t those who have enjoyed ministerial posts in the state government thanks to Ajit Dada think the ring road in Pune should be named after him?" he said.He warned that if the government did not announce the naming of the road, his party would launch a major agitation on Ajit Pawar's death anniversary to press for the demand.Rohit Pawar also said efforts would continue to establish whether the former deputy CM's death was an accident or a conspiracy.Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport. The aircraft was flying from Mumbai to Baramati. Four others were also killed in the crash.The Maharashtra CID and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Union civil aviation ministry, are conducting separate investigations into the incident.Following Ajit Pawar's death, his wife Sunetra Pawar took over as the NCP president and became Maharashtra's deputy chief minister.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar urges Union home minister Amit Shah to announce a CBI probe into the death of the former Maharashtra deputy chief minister. This came as Shah is on a two-day visit to Pune and is set to unveil a statue of AjIt Pawar.

Article Title: Parliament winter session likely in 1st week of December; delimitation bill to be in focus
Article Text:
The government faces a numbers test as it seeks opposition support for the proposed constitutional amendment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The winter session of Parliament is likely to commence in the first week of December, news agency PTI reported on Sunday. The government is looking to secure passage of a Constitution amendment bill linking women's reservation to delimitation. This comes as opposition parties prepare to intensify their protests over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, enabling the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The possible dates are being discussed at the highest levels of the government, PTI reported citing sources.However, the bill faces a significant numbers challenge. A Constitution amendment requires the support of at least two-thirds of members present and voting. In the current Lok Sabha, this translates to 361 votes if all 540 members vote, with three seats vacant.The ruling NDA has 320 members and will need opposition support to cross the required threshold. A senior government functionary, however, expressed confidence on Thursday that the legislation would clear Parliament by a margin of 15 to 18 votes.The legislative push is also likely to coincide with a fresh confrontation between the government and opposition over the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have stepped up their criticism of the electoral roll revision and are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Their protests could spill into the winter session and disrupt parliamentary proceedings.An MP from the ruling alliance said a Constitution amendment bill could not be debated and put to vote unless the House functioned in an orderly manner.Meanwhile, the government's decision not to prorogue the Monsoon session has added to speculation about the next parliamentary sitting. The session was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has remained unprorogued for 94 days, exceeding the previous record of 87 days in 2008.Keeping the session alive has allowed the government to retain the option of convening an extended sitting at short notice. Such a sitting would require a minimum notice of two days, compared with at least 14 days for convening a fresh session.The government is also learnt to be considering a formula to address concerns over the proposed delimitation, particularly those raised by southern states. Under the proposal being explored, Lok Sabha seats could be increased by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census. No final decision has been taken on the framework.The proposed constitutional amendment had failed to secure the required numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17.
Article Summary: The winter session of Parliament is likely to commence in the first week of December. The government is looking to secure passage of a Constitution amendment bill. This comes as opposition parties prepare to intensify their protests over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: IndiGo Guwahati-bound flight returns safely to Pune after landing gear fails to retract
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An IndiGo Airbus A320 (VT-IZE) operating from Pune to Guwahati on Sunday had to return to the origin after its landing gear did not retract after take off. The aircraft with about 200 people on board had taken off at 7.17 am and the pilots discovered they were unable to retract the gear which made it impossible to proceed on the journey. Deciding to return, they contacted Pune air traffic control. As per protocol, the Pune airport, which is an Indian Air Force base, made all emergency preparations for its landing which the aircraft safely did just after 9 am. Flight movement timings are as per Flightradar 24 data.Tanked up for the about three-hour flight, the pilots first flew the aircraft in a hold for about an hour near Pune to burn fuel and get within maximum landing weight. Once there, they then did a low pass over the Pune runway so that air traffic control could visually verify the position of the landing gear gear to confirm to the cockpit that the same is indeed out and that is okay to land. This is done as per protocol to rule out a false indication of landing gear position in the flight deck.An IndiGo spokesperson said: “6E 623 of Nov 15 returned to origin and landed safely at the Pune International Airport after a technical snag was detected shortly after take-off.In line with standard operating procedures, all relevant authorities were immediately informed. The aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks and will resume operations after securing necessary clearances.”“An alternate aircraft has been arranged promptly to operate the flight. We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and are taking all possible measures to minimise it, including offering them regular updates, meals and refreshments, alternate flight options and refunds, as applicable. We thank our customers for their patience and understanding. At IndiGo, the safety and comfort of our customers and crew remain our top priority,” the spokesperson added.A flight with landing gear out returns to the origin as continuing the journey will mean increased drag that leads to a much higher fuel burn of about 150%.
Article Summary: An IndiGo Airbus A320 (VT-IZE) operating from Pune to Guwahati had to return to the origin after its landing gear did not retract after take off. The aircraft with about 200 people on board had taken off at 7.17 am and the pilots discovered they were unable to retract the gear.

Article Title: Major accident averted as empty Vande Bharat travels 463 km with faulty brakes
Article Text:
The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi

NEW DELHI: A major accident was averted after an empty Vande Bharat train travelled nearly 463 km with its coaches' braking systems allegedly non-functional, despite repeated warnings from loco pilots. The incident, which took place in October, has prompted the South Eastern Railway (SER) zone to order a probe into multiple safety lapses that could have endangered railway operations.The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh using a freight locomotive. According to PTI, railway staff failed to properly integrate the train's braking system with the locomotive and ignored warnings from the crew before allowing it to continue its journey.The incident came days before the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailment in Assam on November 11, which also raised concerns over alleged negligence in railway operations.In an order dated November 7, the SER zone directed the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Ranchi to investigate the incident and identify those responsible.According to the order, the loco pilot conducted a brake power test after departing from Hatia and found that the braking performance was extremely poor.He submitted a written complaint to railway officials upon reaching Ranchi, but the train was allowed to proceed.Another loco pilot operating the rake from Muri station also alerted the concerned controllers, reporting that the brakes could not be applied by dropping the brake pipe (BP) pressure.It was only when the train reached Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) station in Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli district that officials inspected the rake. They found that the braking systems of all coaches had been isolated, rendering them ineffective.The preliminary probe identified alleged negligence by coach and wagon maintenance staff, section and traction controllers, as well as the train crew. It noted that maintenance staff had failed to physically verify the brakes before departure, while the crew's unfamiliarity with the Vande Bharat's braking system also contributed to the lapse.
Article Summary: The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh. South Eastern Railway (SER) zone has ordered a probe into multiple safety lapses that could have endangered railway operations.

Article Title: Faith, pollution and politics: How Yamuna takes centre stage every Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Significance of Chhath

Chhath and politics go hand in hand in Delhi

Why Chhath has become a political event

Why the Yamuna turns frothy around Chhath

The health risks for the devotees

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja . With God as their witness - quite literally in this case - devotees go to great lengths to observe strict hygiene while following elaborate rituals centred around the worship of the Sun deity over four days.In Delhi, however, devotees will step into the sullied waters of the Yamuna, believing that their faith will protect them.As Delhi is already gasping for breath after Diwali, the debate has now pivoted to the pollution of the river which Delhi, for most of the year, views from the bridges built over it.As thousands of people come down to the Yamuna's banks, the river will undergo its annual public audit by devotees standing waist-deep in its waters.Chhath Puja, rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand.Observed over four days, the festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees prepare simple, traditional food while observing strict personal hygiene and purity.This is followed by Kharna, when jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis are prepared as prasad.After Kharna, devotees undertake a rigorous 36-hour nirjala fast, abstaining from both food and water.The rituals culminate in offerings of arghya to the setting Sun, followed by prayers to the rising Sun on the final day.Every year, as Chhath Puja approaches, the Yamuna becomes more than a river for Delhi.This year, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the cleanup under chief minister Rekha Gupta.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here?” he said. “There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water.”AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar answered by floating an effigy of Tiwari at Kalindi Kunj and challenging him to bathe there, claiming that stretch was far more polluted.On Nahay Khay, the first day of the festival, a video purportedly showing dead fish near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media.Delhi ministers accused AAP of staging it, alleging that party workers bought fish from the market and dumped them in the river.Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj denied this and demanded an inquiry on Friday, saying water samples had not yet been collected to establish the cause.The river has been a political flashpoint around Chhath before. Last year, AAP alleged that a temporary artificial pool at Vasudev Ghat was built to project a clean Yamuna ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s planned Chhath visit, which did not take place.Chhath's growing political importance has a lot to do with Delhi's changing demography. According to reports, continued migration from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP has increased the share of the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of Delhi's population.The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency through a celebration deeply woven into its cultural identity.According to reports, the Delhi government is setting up 1,482 Chhath ghats across 996 locations. The growing prominence of a festival once largely observed within community networks reflects how it has become an important fixture on the capital's political calendar.The Yamuna's pollution becomes particularly visible around Chhath Puja, when devotees gather in large numbers along its banks to offer prayers.While talking to the Times of India, environmentalist Saumya Dutta said that the timing of Chhath coincides with a period when the river's flow has receded considerably after the monsoon, leaving less water to dilute the pollutants entering it.“During the days of Chhath Puja, tens of thousands of Delhi residents from Bihar and eastern UP, along with others, add huge amounts of pollutants, particularly detergents containing surfactants, which are common ingredients in soaps and detergents, as well as some industrial waste,” Dutta said.“Long after the peak monsoon flow, this is the period when the Yamuna's flow becomes very low. This low water flow, combined with high amounts of surfactants, causes large amounts of foam when the water is agitated. This becomes particularly visible during the huge influx of people and pollutants into this short 2% stretch of the Yamuna,” he said.According to Dutta, the 22-km stretch through the capital accounts for roughly 2% of the Yamuna's total length but contributes 70-80% of its overall pollution load.“Defaming agents and pre-Chhath cleaning do help for a very short period, but as the incoming pollution does not go down, this benefit is very short-term and vanishes quickly,” Dutta told TOI.“The major reason for the abject failure of Yamuna cleaning plans, as well as schemes like Namami Gange, is that the huge daily inflow of partially treated or even untreated sewage and industrial effluent into the river is not being tackled,” he added.In one of the most polluted major rivers of India, devotees will stand waist-deep, waiting for the Sun to set and rise the following day.But is it safe for a person to come in contact with such polluted river?According to Dr Srijan Garg immersion during Chhath can expose people to harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites through the skin, eyes, nose and ears, and sometimes through accidental ingestion."Devotees are exposed through the skin, eyes, nose, ear and sometimes by ingestion. However, the major exposure is through the skin and can cause various infections such as folliculitis, dermatitis, fungal infections," Dr. Garg told TOI.The water is full of untreated sewage water. so swallowing that water will affect the health of the individual. Some acute infections typhoid, hepatitis A or E, giardiasis, cholera. These usually present with diarrhoea, vomiting and pain abdomen," he added.Meanwhile, Dr. Ishan Singh said that people with cuts or open wounds are particularly vulnerable to infections."Industrial discharge may introduce heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium into river water. Depending on concentration and duration of exposure, these can affect the kidneys, liver and nervous system. Some chemicals may also irritate the skin and eyes," Dr. Singh told TOI."However, their actual presence and concentration at individual ghats must be confirmed through laboratory testing. A single brief exposure should not automatically be considered a cause of heavy-metal poisoning," he added.He also said that children, pregnant women, elderly people, diabetic patients and people with weakened immunity need particular attention.Dr. Singh also advised devotees to avoid swallowing river water, keep immersion time short and stay away from areas close to sewage discharge points. Those with open wounds should preferably avoid entering the water. After immersion, devotees should wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and change out of wet clothes.Chhath will end with prayers to the rising Sun, as devotees complete the four-day rituals with hopes and gratitude. However, the Yamuna's problems will remain long after the devotees leave the ghats.The wait for a cleaner river is likely to continue, with sewage and industrial waste flowing into it despite periodic cleaning drives and political promises.And when Chhath returns next year, the river will once again face its annual public audit, with the same questions over its cleanliness and safety likely to resurface.
Article Summary: Chhath Puja is rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. It is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand. The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025.The last visit by a Pakistani minister to India was in May 2023, when then Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari travelled to Goa to attend a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Musadik Masood Malik, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, will lead the country’s delegation to the dialogue.India had invited culture minister Aurangzeb Khichi for the event. Musadik Masood Malik, federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, will lead the team. He however, is considered a more experienced minister in the Pakistan govt. "The event will bring together representatives from SCO member states to exchange views on issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding," said Pakistan in its announcement, adding that Islamabad remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people ties within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect.After Bilawal's visit in 2023, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had visited Pakistan the next year, again for a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting between the ministers.Even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement for over a decade, both countries have continued to interact within the Eurasian bloc which they both joined as full members in 2017.Pakistan currently holds the SCO presidency and will host the heads of state summit next year. In the current circumstances, Modi's participation in it is unlikely as India's position - that talks and terror can't go hand in hand - has hardened further after the Pahalgam attack.
Article Summary: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.

NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said the law was on the state's side in the ongoing dispute over the proposed Mekedatu dam project on the Cauvery river . Kharge went on to add that that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu would have to abide by the Supreme Court 's directions."The Tamil Nadu PCC president will make statements and do everything within his capacity to protect Tamil Nadu's interests. Similarly, the Karnataka PCC president, the Chief Minister and all of us are duty-bound to protect our state's interests," he said.He further added: "Irrespective of our individual views, the Supreme Court has given directions, and the law is on our side. Whatever happens, it is going to benefit both states. In fact, Mr Shivakumar had offered the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister an opportunity to have a dialogue on this... Everyone has to follow the law of the land".His remarks come amid a row over the project, with the BJP accusing the Congress of adopting different positions in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Senior BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Karnataka Assembly, R Ashoka, on Sunday alleged that the Congress was using the state's water rights for political gains while its leaders in Tamil Nadu were opposing the project.Ashoka pointed to Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B Manickam Tagore's description of the Mekedatu project as illegal and his appeal to chief minister C Joseph Vijay to take legal steps to prevent its implementation. He also cited Tamil Nadu Congress MP Jothimani's opposition to the project.Accusing the Congress of double standards, Ashoka said the party had earlier organised a Mekedatu padayatra in Karnataka under the slogan 'Our water, our right', but had remained silent over opposition from its leaders in Tamil Nadu."Padayatra in Karnataka, legal battle in Tamil Nadu! Slogans in support of Kannadigas in Karnataka, a fight against the rights of Kannadigas in Tamil Nadu! What should one call this double standard of the Congress?" he said in a post on X.On Saturday, Shivakumar had reiterated the Karnataka government's commitment to pursuing the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, maintaining that the state had the right to build the dam while protecting Tamil Nadu's share of Cauvery water.He said Karnataka would seek the necessary clearances and proceed in accordance with the Supreme Court's directions.What is the Mekedatu project?The Mekedatu project is a proposed multi-purpose balancing reservoir across the Cauvery river near Kanakapura in Karnataka's Bengaluru South district. It is intended to meet Bengaluru's drinking water requirements and generate hydroelectric power.Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed the project, expressing concerns that its implementation could affect the state's share of Cauvery water.
Article Summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said the law was on the state's side. Kharge went on to add that that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu would have to abide by the Supreme Court's directions. His remarks come amid a row over the project, with the BJP accusing the Congress of adopting different positions.

PUNE: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight (6E 0623) with 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, reported a technical issue shortly after take-off.The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraft’s landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off and remained in the extended position. Airport officials said that immediately upon receiving the information, they coordinated with ATC, IndiGo and all concerned agencies."The Indian Air Force (IAF) declared a Full Emergency, following which all prescribed emergency response procedures were promptly activated. Fire services, ambulance services and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to ensure the safety of passengers and crew," Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke said.As a precautionary measure, the aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am."Following the landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay number- 7 by three fire-fighting vehicles and two ambulances, in accordance with the prescribed emergency response procedures.After confirmation of the aircraft’s safe and normal status, ATC declared the full emergency withdrawn at 9.10am. Thereafter, the aerobridge was connected, and all passengers were safely deboarded," the director added.All 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, were safe, and no injuries were reported. IndiGo is arranging an alternate aircraft from Bengaluru to Pune to facilitate the onward journey of the affected passengers to Guwahati.
Article Summary: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight reported a technical issue. The pilot informed Air Traffic Control that the aircraft’s landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off. The aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am.

Article Title: Air India Delhi-SFO was 2.5 hours away from destination when US ATC failed; all 5 AI flights landed on time

NEW DELHI: Air India ’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination, when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th when Uncle Sam’s outdated air traffic control (ATC) systems began to fail. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. Luckily, the US Air Traffic Control System Command Centre (ATCSCC) advisory issued at 2.24 am (IST of Nov 14) to announce the ground stop said “inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis” while asking all departing flights to remain on ground. The Boeing 777 (VT-ALS) landed in SFO at 5 am.“As soon as the ATCSCC advisory was issued at 2.24 am, AI flight operations buzzed the leadership team and they went into a huddle. SFO flight was the closest to its destination and proceeded since the pilots, who were in touch with Oakland control at that time, were not told to divert as per the advisory which meant the B777 will be allowed to land,” said people in the know.AI kept a close eye on the developing situation and the four other flights — one each from Delhi and Mumbai to Newark (EWR) and JFK — kept proceeding to their destinations.The outage lasted about five hours and these all landed as per schedule.Of the five return flights these aircraft were to operate back home, only SFO-Delhi (via Kolkata) was delayed by about 2 hours and 40 minutes due to congestion at SFO. “All the other flights, two each out of EWR and JFK, operated on time,” said an official, adding Saturday-Sunday night departures were also on time except for the delayed arrival from SFO.AI senior pilots said this is the second time in less than four years that US faced an air traffic communication issue, although Friday the 13th was by far the most serious one. On Jan 10, 2023, the US Federal Aviation Administration was unable to issue notice to airmen (NOTAM) for some hours and it had to activate a hotline to manage the situation then. The FAA subsequently traced the problem to files unintentionally deleted by contract personnel while correcting synchronisation between the primary and backup databases.Following Friday’s failure, the US is prioritising international flights over domestic ones and the situation will take some days to recover as there will be a serious ripple effect. While Air India is the only Indian operator that flies to the US, two US carriers — United and American — have a daily each between Delhi and New York. Rest of the connectivity is provided by onestops of Gulf, European and southeast Asian carriers.Other airlines’ flights were also impacted.“Given the scale of the failure, the impact was massive. I was listening to ground control at JFK when the issue happened just before 4 pm EST (New York time) Friday. There were a lot of frustrated pilots and controllers. Hundreds of pilots were asking, ‘what’s the delay reason,’. Initially controller couldn’t give a reason and just said, ‘nationwide stop.’ Later it was determined a communication problem,” said a pilot who was in New York at that time.“Due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety, attention all aircraft operators: By order of the Federal Aviation Command Centre, all airports are ground stopped,” the ATCSCC advisory announcing the failure had said.
Article Summary: Air India’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time.

NEW DELHI: India's ambassador to US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Saturday hit back at the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), saying it had "no locus standi" to comment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.His remarks came after the commission described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as a person detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.In a strongly worded post on X, Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment and accused it of making partisan and ill-informed remarks about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights."USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Kwatra said."India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. The relief came with conditions barring him from using social media, interacting with media persons or meeting anyone other than family members, relatives and friends.Established by the US government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the US State Department.

NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in front of others to late-night humiliation and social boycotts - has prompted National Medical Commission (NMC) to issue 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges between Oct 16 and Nov 11.The complaints, received by NMC's anti-ragging cell, concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. Article Title: Studying abroad, visiting India or working overseas? Who gets counted in Census 2027 across UP
Article Text:

LUCKNOW: Indian residents travelling abroad temporarily will be counted at their usual place of residence if they return during the 35-day enumeration period of Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, subject to enumeration rules.The clarification comes ahead of the 15-day online self-enumeration exercise in Uttar Pradesh, beginning Nov 16 and continuing until Nov 30, followed by door-to-door population enumeration from Dec 1, 2026, to Jan 4, 2027.Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas.Indian citizens studying, working or permanently residing abroad throughout the enumeration period would generally not be included in their family's household merely because they hold Indian passports.Parents completing online self-enumeration should therefore not include children ordinarily residing abroad.However, if a temporarily absent family member returns during the enumeration period and qualifies for inclusion, the enumerator can update the household details during the physical visit.Personnel posted at Indian diplomatic missions abroad will be covered through special arrangements coordinated centrally.Conversely, foreign nationals ordinarily residing in India, including students and workers, will be counted irrespective of citizenship. Short-term foreign visitors and diplomatic personnel enjoying immunity are subject to separate rules.Verma emphasised that the census records population, not citizenship, and inclusion does not confer Indian citizenship.Similarly, seasonal migrant workers residing in Uttar Pradesh during enumeration, including those employed at brick kilns, sugar mills and other establishments, will be counted in the state.They should inform enumerators at their places of origin to prevent duplication.The census reference time is midnight at the start of Jan 5, 2027. A revisional round from January 5 to 9 will account for births, deaths and omissions.Final census data is scheduled to be made public in April 2027.
Article Summary: Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas. The clarification comes ahead of the 15-day online self-enumeration exercise in Uttar Pradesh.

Article Title: From odd-even to cloud seeding: Why Delhi's pollution battle remains unfinished
Article Text:
National Capital witnesses health emergency

2024 vs 2026: What changed in strategy?

Rules under AAP

Rules under BJP

Why Delhi keeps choking

Prolonged exposure to toxic air

Seasonal firefighting or lasting solutions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every winter, Delhi's air turns toxic.Governments change, action plans get revamped and new solutions are announced.Yet, the capital continues to battle hazardous air, with residents bearing the health costs of a crisis that refuses to go away.At the time of publishing this article on Saturday (7pm IST), Delhi's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 367, in the ‘very poor’ category, which had breached the ‘severe’ level on Friday.The latest spike came days after Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governments introduced separate action plans and announced a range of measures to tackle Delhi's recurring air pollution crisis during their respective tenures. Both failed.So are successive governments fighting pollution at its source, or merely trying to manage the smog after it sets in?When AAP was in power in Delhi, its 2024 Winter Action Plan focused on a combination of emergency interventions, dust suppression and monitoring of pollution sources.The 21-point plan, announced in September 2024, included drone surveillance of pollution hotspots, a special task force, anti-dust campaigns at construction sites and the deployment of mechanical road sweepers, water sprinklers and mobile anti-smog guns.The odd-even vehicle scheme was another emergency option used by AAP govt to reduce vehicular emissions if air quality deteriorated further.The AAP government's plan also targeted industrial pollution, open waste burning and stubble burning. It called for stricter monitoring of construction sites, action against polluting industrial units and enforcement of pollution-control norms.A ban on firecrackers was announced ahead of Diwali to prevent a seasonal spike in emissions.Following BJP's victory in the February 2025 assembly elections, the new government under chief minister Rekha Gupta introduced a 25-point Air Pollution Mitigation Plan in June, followed by a separate Winter Action Plan in October 2026.Its strategy placed greater emphasis on enforcement against polluting vehicles, construction dust and industrial emissions. Measures included ANPR cameras to identify overage vehicles, restrictions on certain polluting commercial vehicles, expansion of electric public transport and stricter checks at PUC centres. For dust control, the government announced the deployment of 86 mechanical road sweepers, 300 water sprinklers and 362 anti-smog guns under its winter plan.BJP also attempted cloud seeding in October 2025 as an experimental measure to induce artificial rain and wash pollutants out of the air. However, the two trials conducted on October 28 failed to produce rainfall, with insufficient moisture in the clouds cited as the primary reason.A subsequent trial was also called off because of unfavourable atmospheric conditions.This year, the Supreme Court permitted the use of certified green firecrackers during Diwali under limited hours.While emergency interventions such as cloud seeding, smog guns and traffic restrictions are often discussed as possible solutions, environmental experts argue that the problem requires a more sustained, science-led approach. Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalysts, explains why these measures have limited impact and what Delhi needs to address the pollution crisis in the long run.Dahiya said cloud seeding cannot be a reliable solution to Delhi's winter pollution as it requires moisture-laden clouds, which are largely absent during the smog season."You can't seed clouds that aren't there," he said, adding that even if artificial rain is induced, the relief may last only a few hours. Pollution also moves across administrative boundaries and can quickly return due to emissions from the wider Delhi-NCR airshed. "Cloud seeding treats the symptom, at best, for a few hours," he said.On the contribution of vehicles to Delhi's pollution, Dahiya said they remain among the biggest local sources of PM2.5. Citing IITM's real-time data, he said vehicular emissions accounted for 31% of PM2.5 on November 13, making them the largest single direct source. However, he cautioned against relying solely on restrictions without improving public transport."You can't ban your way out if people have no alternative," he said, pointing out that around 6,400 buses with GPS were tracked on Delhi's roads on November 13, below the city's long-standing target.He also questioned the effectiveness of smog guns and water sprinklers in reducing city-wide PM2.5 levels, saying they mainly settle coarse dust over limited areas, while winter pollution is largely driven by fine combustion particles and secondary pollutants.Calling for dust control through paving, covering construction materials and mechanised sweeping, he described spraying water into the air as "visible action, not effective action".The impact of Delhi's recurring pollution crisis goes beyond seasonal coughing, breathlessness and respiratory infections. Doctors warn that prolonged exposure to polluted air can affect lung development in children and increase the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular problems.Dr Nikhil Rajvanshi, Consultant – Pediatric Pulmonologist, Allergy and Sleep Specialist, Rainbow Children's Hospital, Delhi, explains that children inhale more air relative to their body weight than adults, making them particularly vulnerable to pollutants. He warns that children exposed to high pollution levels over several years may experience reduced lung growth and lower lung function as adults. Importantly, even children without diagnosed respiratory conditions are not immune. "Some effects may persist even after exposure decreases," he cautions.Highlighting the wider health implications, Dr Vikas Mittal, Director – Pulmonology, CK Birla Hospital, Delhi, says PM2.5 particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, triggering inflammation across the body. Repeated exposure can worsen asthma and COPD, impair lung function and increase cardiovascular risks, including hypertension, heart attacks and strokes. He also warns that prolonged exposure can cause lasting changes to lung tissue, even among otherwise healthy individuals."Some changes may improve when exposure is reduced, but prolonged injury and remodelling of lung tissue may not be completely reversible," he says.The doctors also highlight the potential consequences of continued exposure over the next five to ten years. Dr Rajvanshi warns that an entire generation of children growing up in highly polluted environments could face reduced peak lung function, increased asthma prevalence and greater susceptibility to respiratory infections in adulthood.Dr Mittal cautions that the consequences would not be limited to people with existing illnesses, as otherwise healthy individuals are also vulnerable to the cumulative effects of prolonged exposure.With the crisis extending beyond Delhi's borders, responsibility cannot rest with one government or one agency alone. It requires coordination between the Centre, Delhi and neighbouring states, along with measurable targets and accountability for missed deadlines.As political parties trade claims over who is responsible for the city's deteriorating air, residents continue to breathe the consequences. Ultimately, the success of any government's pollution plan will not be measured by the number of announcements or anti-smog guns deployed, but by whether Delhi can finally breathe easier, not just in winter, but throughout the year.The scale of the challenge, Dahiya said, cannot be understood by looking at Delhi's borders or the winter stubble-burning season alone.He said stubble burning accounts for less than 5% of Delhi's PM2.5 over a full year, while only around 30% of the city's pollution originates within its boundaries. This makes a regional approach essential, rather than one that focuses only on Delhi or relies on measures activated when AQI levels spike.He called for a regional airshed plan covering the NCR and the Indo-Gangetic plain, with year-round emission-reduction targets for vehicles, industries, power plants, waste, household fuel and dust. "We need targets for how many tonnes each source and each geography must cut, and by when," he said.Dr Mittal says the priority must be controlling pollution at its source through stricter checks on vehicular emissions, industrial pollution, construction dust and crop-residue burning."Clean air is a public health necessity, and controlling pollution at its source remains the most effective long-term solution," he says.So, until action moves beyond seasonal restrictions and visible interventions to measurable reductions in emissions, the capital risks returning to the same cycle of toxic air every winter.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governments introduced separate action plans and announced a range of measures to tackle Delhi's recurring air pollution crisis. At the time of publishing this article on Saturday (7pm IST), Delhi's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 367, in the ‘very poor’ category.

Article Title: After EASA concern, Air India asks crew to remain on board till replacement arrives during Europe fuelling halts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America that take a fuelling halt in Europe since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb, to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them to operate the remaining lag of the flight. The reason: Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers for the process and since passengers remain on board during this time, cabin crew has to be there to announce precautions like keeping seat belts off.There were some instances when the incoming crew left the aircraft immediately on arrival in Europe. This gap in standard operating procedure (SOP) was detected primarily at Vienna during “EU ramp inspection programme” carried out to do “safety assessment of foreign aircraft” (SAFA). Along with cabin condition issues, this led to European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) SAFA score of Air India rising to 2.7, indicating safety-related deficiencies.The same was conveyed to the Indian Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which then swung into action along with AI to rectify the situation. The airline started deploying new or retrofitted aircraft on these routes which largely took care of cabin issues.For fuelling, AI asked its crew to remain on board till the replacement crew arrives.After taking these two steps, AI’s SAFA score has now gone to about 1.4, indicating that the issues that led to the earlier higher score have been largely addressed. “The DGCA did extensive monitoring and ensured AI followed the protocol to a T. Now AI is in the ‘good zone’ of Europe’s SAFA with the score falling from 2.7 earlier to about 1.4,” said people in the know. “Now crew often remains on board for about 1-1.5 hours after landing to oversee the fuelling process till relief crew arrives,” they add.AI’s improved SAFA score comes as a breather for the short-staffed DGCA that has been headed by non-aviation generalists for about two decades now, just ahead of facing an audit by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) from next week. It is also a relief for Air India as it is the only Indian carrier that flies to the US and will be examined closely by FAA for that reason. In operational terms, this should lead to less checks during fuelling stops in Europe and fewer delays on that count during halts there for AI.Refuelling: The SOP is that an engineering team and/or pilots should be in the flight deck when an aircraft is getting refuelled to coordinate with the fuelling staff. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on when fuelling is taking place.The AI circular for pilots, reiterating the incoming set remains on board till it’s replaced by the relief crew. “Before commencing fuelling, the flight deck crew will be informed by engineering. If flight crew are unable to attend the flight deck during refueling, they shall request a qualified engineer to attend the flight deck,” says his circular.It adds: “NO PED (personal electronic devices) NO SMOKING / NO DEVICES / EXIT signs shall be illuminated as an indication to the cabin crew that fuelling is in progress. 'Seat belt' sign must be off. Known high energy equipment such as HF radios shall not be operated (during refuelling).”
Article Summary: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them. Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on during fuelling.

Article Title: 'Embed quality into every stage': Rajnath Singh calls for stricter checks in defence manufacturing

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday called for stronger quality assurance in indigenous defence manufacturing, saying India must move beyond identifying defects and focus on preventing them at every stage of production.Addressing the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation and Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace virtually, Singh said India had made considerable progress in developing its domestic defence capabilities, but warned that growing technological sophistication also brought greater responsibility to ensure reliability."India has made significant progress in strengthening its indigenous defence ecosystem. Our achievements in missile development, naval platforms, aerospace engineering, radar systems, and space applications reflect the growing capabilities of our scientists, engineers, production agencies, and industry partners," he said.Citing the commissioning of INS Vikrant , India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, Singh said the achievement marked an important milestone in the country's defence manufacturing journey.He also pointed to progress in indigenous missile technology and space systems as evidence of India's scientific and industrial capabilities."The commissioning of India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, designed and constructed in India, marked an important milestone in this journey. Our progress in indigenous missile technology and space systems further demonstrates the strength of India's scientific and industrial capabilities," Singh said.However, he cautioned that these achievements must be backed by stringent quality standards across defence production."These achievements are a matter of immense national pride. However, they also place a greater responsibility on us. As our defence system becomes increasingly sophisticated, we must ensure that every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process meets the highest standards of quality and reliability," he said.The Defence Minister said undetected defects could affect the operational availability of military equipment, raise maintenance requirements and reduce its service life. In critical situations, he warned, such flaws could jeopardise the success of a mission."A hidden defect can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce service life of equipment, and in critical situations even jeopardise the success of a mission," he said.Calling for a change in approach, Singh stressed that quality assurance should be integrated into the entire manufacturing process rather than being treated as a measure to identify faults after production."Therefore, we must move beyond a culture that merely identifies defects and develop a culture that actively prevents them. This requires us to embed quality into every stage of the manufacturing process," he added.Singh said the conference theme, ‘Innovation for Strategic and Economic Excellence’, was relevant to India's ambition of becoming technologically advanced, industrially strong, strategically secure and globally competitive."The theme of this conference ', Innovation for Strategic and Economic Excellence', is particularly relevant in the present times. It reflects our aspiration to build an India that is technologically advanced, industrially strong, strategically secure, and globally competitive," Singh said.He added that national progress depended not only on technological development but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems being built, particularly in strategic sectors such as defence."The progress of any nation does not depend merely on the technology it develops. It also depends on the quality, reliability, and security of the system it builds. This becomes particularly important in strategic sectors, such as defence, where the consequences of any failure can be far-reaching," he said.Singh, who said he could not attend the event in person due to viral fever, joined the gathering virtually. He also congratulated the leadership of the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing, the organising committee and others involved in organising the conference."I would like to congratulate the leadership of the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing, the organising committee, and everyone who has worked tirelessly to bring together this prestigious event," he said.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh calls for stronger quality assurance in indigenous defence manufacturing. He says India must move beyond identifying defects and focus on preventing them at every stage of production. Singh said undetected defects could affect operational availability of military equipment, raise maintenance requirements and reduce service life.

Article Title: India opposes UN call for death penalty moratorium, says no global consensus
Article Text:
"Travesty to term" capital punishment "state-inflicted death," said the India rep

India voted against a United Nations General Assembly resolution calling for a global moratorium on the death penalty, maintaining that there is no international consensus against capital punishment and that sovereign states have the right to decide their own laws and penalties.The resolution, which called on countries to move towards abolishing the death penalty, was adopted by the UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Friday. India was among 33 countries that voted against it, while 133 supported the proposal and 16 abstained. The vote was in line with India's position in previous sessions, including in 2016, 2018 and 2024.India also opposed language in a separate resolution on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions that linked the death penalty with torture and ill-treatment. While supporting the broader resolution, New Delhi disassociated itself from one of its paragraphs, arguing that lawful capital punishment following due process should not be equated with unlawful killings.Speaking at the committee, Bhavika Mangalanandan, first secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, said capital punishment was permitted under international law, subject to restrictions."There is no international consensus against capital punishment, and article six of the ICCPR permits its use with restrictions.Capital punishment is meted out after rigorous and due legal process," she said, as quoted by ANI."It is therefore a travesty to term it state-inflicted death," she added.Mangalanandan objected to discussing capital punishment under a resolution dealing with extrajudicial and arbitrary executions, calling the approach "disingenuous and mischievous". She said it sought to present "personal ideological preferences as settled international law".India's objection was specifically to Operational Paragraph 6 of the resolution, which referred to recommendations made by the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions. The paragraph called on states to take those recommendations into account."We strongly disagree with the assertion conveyed in the report of the Special Rapporteur and thereby through the resolution. The death penalty inherently constitutes torture or ill-treatment," Mangalanandan said.Explaining India's position, she said the death penalty was a statutory provision in the country and was imposed only in the "rarest of rare" cases. She also cited procedural safeguards, including the presumption of innocence, mandatory confirmation of death sentences by a higher court and consideration of mitigating circumstances."Extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions are unlawful and a clear violation of human rights," she said, adding that India supported the broader resolution seeking to eradicate such violations.The United States also voted against the death penalty moratorium resolution, saying its language was problematic and that decisions on capital punishment should be left to individual countries' domestic democratic processes, subject to international law.US deputy representative to the UN Economic and Social Council Yaryna Ferencevych said Washington did not consider the lawful use of capital punishment inconsistent with respect for human rights. She also stressed that countries retaining the penalty must ensure fair trials and prohibit execution methods designed to cause undue pain or suffering.France, meanwhile, welcomed the resolution's adoption, describing it as an important step towards the universal abolition of the death penalty.
Article Summary: India voted against a resolution calling for a global moratorium on the death penalty. The resolution was adopted by the UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Friday. New Delhi disassociated itself from one of its paragraphs, arguing that lawful capital punishment following due process should not be equated with unlawful killings.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in electoral rolls while simultaneously addressing inconsistencies in the lists during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise."There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the Commission remains alive to the need to ensure that those who are eligible to vote find their names in the voters' lists but equally, at the same time, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed," the poll panel said in an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, as reported by news agency PTI.The EC said voters whose names were missing from the draft electoral rolls despite being enrolled in previous electoral rolls could apply afresh using Form 6 without facing prosecution, provided they were not already registered in another parliamentary or assembly constituency and their declarations complied with the law.The clarification came after concerns were raised that such applicants could face prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, for submitting Form 6 despite having been registered earlier. The Commission said it had asked chief electoral officers to publicise the clarification widely, including in local languages.According to PTI, the EC also informed the court that it had taken note of its suggestion to reach out to voters categorised as ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate) to facilitate their inclusion in electoral rolls.In a communication dated November 6, 2026, the Commission directed chief electoral officers in states and Union territories where the SIR is underway to allow voters to submit duly filled Enumeration Forms to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Booth Level Officer (BLO) at their current ordinary residence.Voters who have not shifted can submit a signed Enumeration Form along with a statement explaining why they had not submitted it earlier. The documents can be submitted personally or through family members. An online submission facility with e-sign is also available on ECINET.The EC said it had directed the creation of a mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector was deprived of an opportunity to have their name included in the final electoral roll, while also preventing duplicate registrations.The Commission said the exercise involved challenges because of the large number of voters and the digitalisation of electoral data. It maintained that ensuring the purity of the electoral process and protecting the voting rights of eligible citizens remained its constitutional responsibility.
Article Summary: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in electoral rolls. It said voters whose names were missing from the draft electoral rolls despite being enrolled in previous electoral rolls could apply afresh using Form 6.

NEW DELHI: Govt has opened applications for companies to become consent managers under India's data protection law. Once registered, these firms will be able to offer a website or app where users can review the permissions they have given to participating businesses and grant or withdraw consent.For users, the service could bring permissions from several businesses into one place. For instance, a user could review a data request from one company and withdraw an earlier permission given to another through the same app, if both businesses are on the platform.Consent managers will have to give users access to their consent history, including requests they declined and permissions they withdrew. Rules require firms to keep these records for at least seven years, put safeguards in place to prevent data breaches and avoid conflicts of interest with the businesses whose requests they handle.The registration framework under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act took effect on Nov 13. Electronics and IT secretary S Krishnan launched the application portal. Companies incorporated in India with a net worth of at least Rs 2 crore can apply. The Data Protection Board of India will assess whether applicants have the technical, operational and financial capacity to provide the service and publish a list of firms it registers.Govt is implementing the law in phases. Key provisions covering users' rights, companies' obligations and board's powers to conduct inquiries and impose penalties will take effect from May 13, 2027.
Article Summary: Govt has opened applications for companies to become consent managers under India's data protection law. Once registered, these firms will be able to offer a website or app where users can review the permissions they have given to participating businesses. For users, the service could bring permissions from several businesses into one place.
